newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Maoists quit uprising, join death squad.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Maoists quit uprising, join death squad.

text.p: A group of Maoist rebels in southern Colombia said on Wednesday they were abandoning their revolutionary struggle to side with right-wing paramilitary death squads.

In a communique made available to Reuters, a 48-strong guerrilla front based in southern Narino and Putumayo provinces blamed their decision to quit the People's Liberation Army (EPL), Colombia's third largest rebel force, on debilitating internal power struggles.
"The crisis within the EPL sparked by bad financial management and the abandonment of our guiding principles has led to an internal struggle for power," the document said.

The EPL deserters said they would join the country's most- feared paramilitary group, the so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba. More than 300 EPL fighters have laid down their arms since July.

Military experts say EPL morale has been sapped by lack of solid ideological beliefs, the internal battle for power and territorial disputes with the country's largest rebel army, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).

Rebels who abandon the armed struggle are theoretically reincorporated into civil society but human rights groups have claimed there is a lack of control and many join paramilitary groups fighting a low-scale war against the guerrillas.

The country's main paramilitary forces held a summit last month and in a memorandum said they would be trying to regain rebel-controlled areas in 1997, including Putumayo. The military also recently announced it would create a new counterinsurgency battalion in the province, where 27 troops were killed and 60 captured in a devastating rebel attack on Aug. 30.
